items.title: Happy 20th Birthday, Amazon EC2
items.description: On the 20th Anniversary, we recognize how AWS has continued to push the boundaries of what cloud computing can deliver, building custom silicon for general-purpose and AI workloads and expanding EC2 into new form factors and deployment models that our customers in 2006 could not have imagined.

items.title: AWS Glue 6.0 now available with 30% lower price and full Apache Iceberg v3 support
items.description: AWS Glue 6.0 is built on a fully modernized runtime, Apache Spark 4.1, Python 3.13, and Scala 2.13, delivering 30% lower pricing than previous AWS Glue versions.

items.title: Runtime instances: persistent compute for production AI agents on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore
items.description: Announcing runtime instances in Amazon Bedrock AgentCore—persistent, managed EC2 infrastructure for production AI agents with multi-agent collaboration, GPU support, and sessions lasting up to 14 days.

items.title: Amazon DynamoDB now supports real-time vector search at any scale
items.description: DynamoDB now supports native vector search with single-digit millisecond latency at 99%+ recall. It is designed for any scale, even trillions of vectors and requires zero infrastructure management.

items.title: Upgrade Amazon EKS clusters with confidence using Kubernetes version rollbacks
items.description: Learn how Kubernetes version rollbacks for Amazon EKS let you reverse cluster upgrades within seven days. This new feature provides a safety net for upgrade failures—no cluster rebuilds required—turning Kubernetes version upgrades into a reversible, low-risk operation.

items.title: Accelerate your infrastructure deployments by up to 4x with AWS CloudFormation Express mode
items.description: AWS CloudFormation speeds up infrastructure deployment with Express mode, enabling AI agents and developers to receive deployment confirmation in seconds and iterate faster. Available in all commercial Regions at no additional cost.

items.title: Amazon EC2 C9g and C9gd instances powered by AWS Graviton5 processors are now available
items.description: Amazon EC2 C9g and C9gd instances, powered by AWS Graviton5, are now generally available. They deliver up to 25% better compute performance than Graviton4-based instances, 5x larger cache, fastest memory of any processor instances in the cloud, and local NVMe storage options (C9gd).

items.title: Run isolated sandboxes with full lifecycle control: AWS Lambda introduces MicroVMs
items.description: AWS launches a new serverless compute primitive, AWS Lambda MicroVMs. VM-level, isolated sandboxes with no shared kernel or resources between sessions. Rapid launch and resume, full lifecycle control, state preservation up to 8 hours, no infrastructure to manage.
